doc.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024

title: Naming pieces: the water theme and Rock Skipping Under the Half Moon
summary: She explains how titles come, using the water-themed album with Jill Townsend and her childhood piece set in Sechelt, B.C.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When do your titles come into play?

My titles. Someone asked — I was on an interview just before this and that same question came up. They were like, “How do you come up with your titles?” And I said well I think again it comes from — I mean again, with commissions there might be something outlined verbally about the piece. For example I just did an album with the Winnipeg Jazz Orchestra with my friend Jill Townsend and we equally wrote the same amount of music and we had a theme. So the themes were pretty easy to get into, the theme was water. That’s a pretty broad theme by the way. And then we were like we are both in Canada, we both grew up on water, we both grew up on opposite coasts. She was from Nova Scotia and I was from B.C. And we both wrote about pieces from each side. So I wrote about a piece off the St. Lawrence River, she wrote a piece off of Nova Scotia, and then we both wrote pieces based off of areas around the Pacific Northwest. So those titles were really fun to come up with. And I had a theme. So I was like, oh water, one thing I’ve always, you know, where’s that place I love to go with water. And one that pops into my head was like being in the place I was born which is Sechelt, British

Columbia. It’s a beautiful — it’s just all view of water and mountains, and hang out with my cousin and learning how to skip rocks. So I was trying to get the idea of rock skipping, getting past three, getting past four, getting past five, and the whole calm kind of feeling of the water lapping on the beach. So I — you know I had a lot to work with there. So it’s called “Rock Skipping Under the Half Moon” because we were always out there just before dinner or just after dinner, and then we were being called in and by then it was so dark we couldn’t skip rocks anymore. So that’s a story. And then I have a story —
